speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I am Dr. Agent; please tell me, how many hours old is your newborn and were you born prematurely?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born at 33 weeks of gestation. The newborn is presenting with respiratory distress 2 hours after birth. The mother had an uneventful pregnancy until premature onset of labor. There was no significant prenatal care history mentioned.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Since the baby is premature at 33 weeks and presenting with respiratory distress just two hours after birth, could you describe the specific signs you are observing, such as the rate of breathing or any color changes like cyanosis?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Grunting, Intercoastal and subcostal retractions, Peripheral cyanosis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The clinical picture of a 33-week preterm infant with respiratory distress, grunting, and retractions shortly after birth is highly suggestive of respiratory distress syndrome. To confirm this, I need to see the lung imaging.

REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_XRay
REQUEST TEST: Arterial_Blood_Gas_Analysis

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Chest_Radiograph: Fine reticular granulation with ground glass appearance on both lungs; Blood_Gases: pH 7.30 (slightly acidic), PaCO2 50 mmHg (elevated), PaO2 60 mmHg (reduced), HCO3- 24 mEq/L

speaker: Doctor
text:
The chest X-ray showing a ground-glass appearance combined with the history of prematurity and respiratory distress confirms a diagnosis of Respiratory Distress Syndrome.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Neonatal Respiratory Distress Syndrome (NRDS)
